one_liner: Lua-scripted cross-platform build tool with built-in package manager; beats CMake+Make, roughly matches plain Ninja.
what_it_does: Xmake is a standalone build tool and package manager: targets are described in an xmake.lua file (a Lua-based DSL) instead of CMakeLists.txt, and xmake directly executes the resulting build graph rather than generating input for a separate build step. It bundles a package manager (xmake-repo, ~500 packages, plus passthrough to Conan/vcpkg/Conda/Homebrew/Apt/Pacman/Cargo/NuGet/etc.), toolchain auto-detection for dozens of compilers/languages, and optional distributed/remote compilation plus a local/remote build cache. It can also emit CMakeLists.txt, Ninja files, compile_commands.json, or Visual Studio projects for other tools to consume, but does not import an existing CMakeLists.txt/Makefile automatically.
how_it_is_fast: xmake's core engine (xmake-core, written in C, bundled with a modified Lua/tbox runtime) parses xmake.lua and runs the resulting dependency DAG directly in one process and one invocation, the same way Ninja does, instead of the two-stage 'generate Makefiles, then run recursive make' path CMake+Make requires. The measured speedup is specifically against that generate+make baseline (~1.24-1.36x at -j12, ~1.08-1.15x at -j1); xmake does not claim to beat Ninja's own scheduler and is measurably not doing so here. It also ships an optional content-based local/remote build cache (not exercised in this particular benchmark).
when_to_use: Migrating off raw CMake+Make (not CMake+Ninja) where a single tool that configures and builds without a separate generate step is the goal
Want a built-in cross-platform package manager instead of wiring vcpkg/conan into CMake by hand
Targeting niche platforms/toolchains in one config file (WDK drivers, CUDA, Zig, Rust, embedded compilers like Keil/IAR/TI, arbitrary cross toolchains) that CMake supports poorly
New small-to-medium C/C++ project where xmake.lua's terser syntax is a feature rather than a migration cost
Want distributed/remote build or a build cache without separately standing up distcc/ccache/sccache
when_not_to_use: Project already builds via CMake+Ninja or Meson: per this same README, xmake is on par with or slightly slower than plain Ninja, so there is no measured win there
Team depends on CMake's mature IDE/CI/third-party tooling ecosystem; xmake's own IDE plugins (VSCode/Sublime/IDEA/Zed) are official but far smaller in adoption
Large existing CMake codebase: there is no automatic CMakeLists.txt -> xmake.lua converter in this repo, so migration means hand-porting build logic
Treating the claimed multiplier as portable: this is a first-party, tier-C benchmark with no CPU model, OS version, or compiler/flags disclosed
Need airtight incremental-build correctness across all language backends: open issues report gaps for at least one backend (see gotchas)

integration.form: CLI binary (not a library) — precompiled install via curl/wget/PowerShell script or OS package managers
integration.dependencies: none to install (self-contained binary); requires whatever C/C++/other-language toolchain the project itself needs (GCC/Clang/MSVC/etc.), which xmake detects rather than provides
integration.min_toolchain: not documented as a minimum — no dependencies outside the standard library per README; current release v3.1.1 (2026-08-27); source-build requirements (compiler for xmake-core, Lua) not stated in README
integration.platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD/DragonflyBSD, Solaris, Android, iOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, MSYS/MinGW/Cygwin, Wasm, Haiku, HarmonyOS, and arbitrary cross-toolchains, each with multiple listed architectures
integration.thread_safety: not documented — it is a build orchestrator, not a library; parallel job scheduling (-j) is internal to the tool
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — projects are described in the xmake.lua DSL, not consumed directly from an existing CMakeLists.txt/Makefile; xmake can generate CMake/Ninja/VS project files as output but there is no documented importer for existing CMake projects

gotchas: The repo's default branch is 'dev', not 'master'; benchmark_url points at master but the same numbers appear on dev's README

README's headline claim is 'on par with Ninja' — in this exact benchmark table xmake (12.264s parallel / 39.937s single, macOS) is slower than plain ninja (11.327s / 38.995s), so 'faster' here means faster than CMake+Make, not faster than Ninja
Benchmark hardware is described only as '8core' with no CPU model, OS version, or compiler/flags disclosed

Open issues report incremental-build gaps for at least one language backend ('rust project not being rebuilt when modified', #4790) and occasional flaky build failures fixed only by restarting (#4796); verify incremental correctness for your specific toolchain before relying on it
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued siblings are direct substitutes: ccache caches compiler invocations and composes with any build system including xmake; Mill/Buck2 target JVM/Meta monorepo ecosystems, not general C/C++; tup targets the specific pathology of huge (100k-file) trees with slow no-op/rebuild checks under Make. Pick xmake over CMake+Make when you also want a bundled package manager and one-file multi-language config, but pick tup instead if your real bottleneck is Make's no-op/rebuild-check cost at large scale, since xmake's own numbers show it merely tying Ninja rather than tup's claimed order-of-magnitude jump.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README benchmark building xmake's own in-repo xmake-core (C) target: on Termux (8-core, -j12) xmake finished in 24.890s vs cmake(gen+make)'s 5.416s+28.473s=33.889s total (~1.36x), but plain ninja ran in 25.682s, barely behind xmake; on macOS (8-core, -j12) xmake was 12.264s vs cmake(gen+make)'s 1.203s+14.030s=15.233s total (~1.24x), while plain ninja was faster than xmake at 11.327s. Single-threaded (-j1) gaps vs cmake+make were smaller (~1.08-1.15x). Exact CPU model and compiler/flags are not stated.
status_note: Actively maintained: last commit 2026-09-22, latest release v3.1.1 (2026-08-27), 259 open issues, 12.2k stars, no open security advisories found; Apache-2.0 licensed and distributed as a self-contained precompiled binary, so it's cheap to adopt or vendor.
